# Chakri

> Chakri is the Diwali party game: a free web game by the product studio 9io, for Diwali night, played in the browser on one phone passed around the room. It has two games, Jodi Check (a 12-question quiz for two) and Chakri Truth or Dare (2 to 12 players). English first, with a Hinglish switch. No app to install, no sign-up, no ads, and nothing anyone types leaves the phone. Live at https://chakri.9io.ai/ since 29 October 2026.

## Jodi Check

- "How well do you really know each other?" Two players, 12 questions, one phone.
- Choose the jodi: Couple, Siblings ("Bhai Dooj ready"), Best friends or Family. Five of the 12 questions come from that jodi's own set and seven from questions for everyone.
- One player answers six questions about themselves in secret; the other guesses each answer from the same four options; then they swap. Every match lights a diya, and all 12 finish the rangoli.
- Titles by score: 12 Made in the same factory; 10 to 11 Kaju katli jodi; 7 to 9 Gulab jamun jodi; 4 to 6 Soan papdi jodi ("Passed around for years. Never actually opened."); 1 to 3 Same Wi-Fi, different worlds; 0 Strangers at the same party. The better guesser wins bragging rights.

## Chakri Truth or Dare

- 2 to 12 players with the phone in the middle. Swipe the chakri (or tap Spin) and it stops on someone. It never picks the same player twice running, and players who have had fewer turns are likelier.
- The player picks a patakha: Sparkler (easy truth, 1 point), Anaar (juicy truth, 2), Rocket (dare, 2) or Sutli bomb (big dare, 3).
- Everyone has three laddoos; skipping a card costs one, and with none left you have to do it.
- Decks: Family ("Safe in front of Dadi"), Friends ("No mercy"), Couple ("A little spicy, just the two of you", exactly two players only) and Aunty Special ("Nosy relatives, live").
- There's no fixed number of rounds. End game shows the Patakha of the night (most points), the scores and up to three awards: Rocket of the night, Laddoo lover and Laddoo hoarder.

## Key facts

- 82 Jodi Check questions and 176 truth-or-dare cards, each in English and Hinglish (Hindi and English in Roman letters, written so no line assumes a player's gender).
- About the social side of Diwali: sweets, lights, family, nosy relatives, card nights and the soan papdi box that gets passed around. No dare involves fire, firecrackers, diyas, drink, smoke, going outside or messaging anyone outside the room. The Couple deck is flirty, never explicit.
- Results come as 1080 × 1920 story cards to share, send on WhatsApp or save.
- Privacy: no accounts; the browser on that phone keeps only settings: the language, the sound setting, the last names typed, the chosen decks or jodi, and recently played questions.
- Built with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules: SVG art drawn in code, sounds synthesised with Web Audio, no framework or dependencies.
- Developer: 9io (https://9io.ai/). More games: https://9io.ai/games
